items: Do you work or are you a student?
Why did you choose that subject or that kind of work?
What do you enjoy most about your studies or your job?
Would you like to change to a different subject or job in the future?
What do you like most about the place where you grew up?
Has your hometown changed much in recent years?
Would you recommend your hometown to someone who was visiting your country?
What kind of music do you like listening to?
When during the day do you usually listen to music?
Did you learn to play a musical instrument when you were a child?
Do you think people's taste in music changes as they get older?

cueCard.topic: Describe a useful skill you learned from an older person.
bullets: when and where you learned it
who taught it to you and how they taught you
and explain why this skill has been useful to you.

rounding: Do you still use this skill today?
Would you like to teach this skill to someone else one day?

items: What kinds of skills do you think young people most need to learn today?
Why do you think some traditional skills are gradually disappearing in modern societies?
How is the way people learn practical skills today different from the way their grandparents learned them?
Do you think older workers or younger workers have more to offer an employer?
How do you think technology will change the way we learn new skills over the next twenty years?
Do you think schools in the future will still teach practical skills such as cooking or sewing?
